routes.name: Vatican citizenship (tied to office or residence)
routes.summary: Not by birth, descent or naturalization. You become a citizen through authorized stable residence in Vatican City because of an office or job, or by the Pope's permission. It ends when the office or residence ends.

other: Cardinals living in Vatican City or Rome, people who must live there for their office or job, or people the Pope authorizes to reside permanently.
Spouse, children, parents and siblings who live with a citizen and are authorized to reside also become citizens.
Loss is immediate when the qualifying reason ends.

citizenship.note: Can be held alongside the citizenship of your state of origin. Former Italians regain Italian citizenship when they lose it.

routes.name: Authorized residence in Vatican City
routes.summary: Living in Vatican City needs authorization linked to an office or job. The Pope or Cardinal Secretary of State authorizes for Curia-related people, the Governor for others. No general residence visa exists.

other: Entry to the territory is through Italy, so Schengen and Italian rules apply. Not confirmed on an official page here.
